My family has farmed this land for generations. I do what my father showed me, and what I have watched work in my own fields for fifty years. I do not read books. I do what works.

My 6 mu — I put 4 mu into cotton and 2 mu into spring maize. Cotton makes the money. Maize we eat and feed to animals. That is how I always split it.

For the **maize**: I plough in spring before planting. I use hybrid seed — everybody around here uses that kind now, the yields are much better than the old seed we used to keep. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting, maybe half a bag of urea when the stalks get tall and another small handful when the tassels come. I water maybe 4 times — before planting, when it gets knee high, when it flowers, and when the ears are filling. I spray twice, once for the borers when they show up. I get around 600 jin per mu if the rains are okay.

For the **cotton**: Cotton is hard work. I plough it deep in spring. I use improved seed — the kind the village dealer sells, most people here buy the same. Cotton needs feeding a lot, especially when it is setting bolls — I put urea on it 2 or 3 times through summer. I water 5 times. The bugs are always a problem — aphids early, then bollworms — so I spray 5 or 6 times. Last year I got about 260 jin of seed cotton per mu. This year I hope for 280.

If my son had not gone to the city to work, I would hire someone to help pick cotton. Now it is just me and my wife.
